input.command:
cd /private/var/folders/kp/vdv61pd97vd0x29b257r8h7h0000gn/T/barcode-vbuql7bb; cat > /private/tmp/claude-501/-private-var-folders-kp-vdv61pd97vd0x29b257r8h7h0000gn-T-barcode-vbuql7bb/59a2fdef-60ed-4196-a3a0-518414450ac9/scratchpad/c.py <<'EOF'
import numpy as np, subprocess
from PIL import Image
b=np.array(Image.open('barcode.png').convert('RGB')).astype(float).mean(0)
N=len(b)
for L in 'ABCDEFGHIJ':
    out=subprocess.run(['ffmpeg','-v','quiet','-i',f'videos/{L}.mp4','-vf','scale=8:8,fps=2','-f','rawvideo','-pix_fmt','rgb24','-'],capture_output=True).stdout
    f=np.frombuffer(out,np.uint8).reshape(-1,64,3).mean(1)
    idx=np.linspace(0,len(f)-1,N).astype(int)
    v=f[idx]
    print(L,np.abs(v-b).mean(), np.corrcoef(v.ravel(),b.ravel())[0,1])
EOF

content.text:
The barcode matches option B, Becky G ft. Bad Bunny's "Mayores." To check, I made the same kind of barcode for each of the ten videos in `videos/`. I took a frame every half second, averaged its color, and stretched the sequence to the barcode's width. Then I compared each one to `barcode.png` stripe by stripe.

| Option | Average color difference (0–255 scale) | Correlation with the barcode |
|---|---|---|
| **B. Mayores** | **4.8** | **0.86** |
| F. Taki Taki | 25.4 | 0.04 |
| H. Criminal | 27.6 | −0.08 |
| J. Chantaje | 29.9 | −0.03 |
| All others | 41–81 | 0.31 or lower |

B is the only video that tracks the barcode closely. Its colors are almost the same, and its pattern of color changes follows the stripes. None of the other videos come close on either measure.

Answer: B
